_comment: USER-REPORTED TWICE. First: 'The problem is that it chooses to go to the next turn after living
wish, which is incorrect.' Then, after a fix that only LABELLED the offending plan: 'That Living
Wish problem where it skips to T4 in the viewer still seems to exist.' It did.
THE BOARD is EldraziDisplacerFlicker's real turn 3 on seed 1 after the ramp opener (Aether Hub
under two Wild Growths, Conservatory, Mariposa as the land drop). Conservatory is the board's
ONLY white source, and Trace of Abundance's {R/W} pip needs it. So the two orderings of the same
two casts are not equivalent:
* Trace FIRST  -- pays {R/W} off Conservatory, then Living Wish off the rest. Both resolve.
* Wish FIRST   -- spends Conservatory on the Wish, Trace is then unpayable and is DROPPED.
WHY LABELLING WAS NOT ENOUGH, which is the whole point of this fixture. CheckLine prefers the
candidate whose cast sequence equals the human's queued ORDER. The human queues Wish-then-Trace,
so the DROPPING ordering matched their order exactly while the working one matched only the
multiset -- order preference was outranking actually making the casts. The line resolved to
three variants, all three of which silently dropped Trace, and the turn ended after Living Wish.
The fix filters candidates that drop a DECLARED cast before the order preference runs, inside
CheckLine only. Enumeration is untouched: a guard that DELETED dropping orderings moved
Dragonstorm's GT (5 cells, 99 play-changed), and scoping that deletion to human play broke a
saved reference (StompySurprise/claude_s9_gi8). Only the choice among already-matching variants
moves here, and only when the human named the dropped card.
WHY THE COUNT ASSERTION IS NOT ENOUGH EITHER. There were three variants before the fix and three
after -- a different three. `expect_variants: 3` passes on the BROKEN engine, so this fixture
would have been vacuous with it alone. `expect_variants_all_contain` pins WHICH three: every
surviving variant must be a Trace-FIRST ordering. Verified discriminating -- neutralise the
filter and all three variants read 'cast: Living Wish, Trace of Abundance' and this fails.
`choose` rather than `accept` is correct and is not the bug: the human named the two casts but
not WHICH land Trace enchants, and the three surviving variants are the three legal hosts.
MTG_UNPRUNED is required. The cast-ORDERING search is gated on it (UnprunedGate::SearchOrder),
which is exactly how the viewer runs -- without it there are no ordering variants at all and the
fixture would test nothing. energy_counters 0 because the real line spent Aether Hub's ETB
energy on turn 1; with energy the Hub could make white itself and the dilemma would not exist.
validate_line: land=Mariposa Military Base;cast=Living Wish;cast=Trace of Abundance
